Use the masked arrays above and variances $\sigma_v=\alpha_vs$, where $\boldsymbol\alpha$ is any permutation of $(1,11/10,11/10)$.

Let $A_0,A_1,A_2$ be finite arrays on the lattice $u_i=ih$, with the norms $n_v$ defined in the heat-flow preliminaries.
Let the edge joining $v,w$ have array $B$, indexed in the original endpoint order $(0,1)$, and let the edge joining $v,2$ have array $E$, indexed in the order $(v,2)$.

Suppose that $\mu_{a,b,k}(\xi)$ is constant in $(a,b)$ on every cell of one finite rectangular partition, independent of $\xi$ and common to all $k$.

Suppose its values on these cells are bounded measurable functions of $\xi$, and that $$\label{eq:frequency-continuous-condition}
 |\mu_{a,b,k}(\xi)|\leq C_1,

outputs.exact_statement:
For every real $r>2$ there is a finite constant $C_r$ such that $$\|V_r(F,G)\|_{L^{3/2}(\mathbb R^2)}
 \le C_r\|F\|_{L^3(\mathbb R^2)}\|G\|_{L^3(\mathbb R^2)}$$ for all complex $F,G\in L^3(\mathbb R^2)$.

On either space, the centered maximal operator satisfies $$\mu\{Mf>\rho\}\le\frac3\rho\|f\|_1,
 \qquad
 \|Mf\|_p^p\le\frac{6p\,2^{p-1}}{p-1}\|f\|_p^p
 \quad(1<p<\infty).$$ Let $g_\sigma(t)=(2\pi\sigma)^{-1/2}e^{-t^2/(2\sigma)}$. There is an absolute constant $C$ such that $$\begin{aligned}
 \sum_m h g_\sigma((m-j)h)|f(m)|
   &\le C M_{\mathbb Z}f(j), &&\sigma\ge h^2,
   \label{eq:discrete-gaussian-maximal}\\
 \int g_\sigma(t)|f(x-t)|\,\mathrm dt
   &\le C M_{\mathbb R}f(x), &&\sigma>0.
   \label{eq:continuous-gaussian-maximal}
\end{aligned}$$

If $P,Q\ge0$ on the same space, $a\ge1$, and $P\le aQ$, then every Hermitian $K$ supported on $P$ is supported on $Q$, and $$\label{eq:matrix-order}
 b_P(K)\ge a^{-1/2}b_Q(K).$$

Let $(\Omega,
u)$ be a probability space and $E$ a fixed subspace of a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space. Suppose $T_\omega\ge0$ and $K_\omega=K_\omega^*$ are measurable matrices, $\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}T_\omega=E$ and $K_\omega$ is supported on $T_\omega$ almost everywhere, and $$\int_\Omega igl(\lVert T_\omegaVert_{\mathrm{op}}
                  +\lVert K_\omegaVert_{\mathrm{op}} igr)\,\,\mathrm d
u(\omega)
 <\infty.$$ Then $\overline T=\int T_\omega\,\,\mathrm d
u$ has support $E$, $\overline K=\int K_\omega\,\,\mathrm d
u$ is supported on $\overline T$, and $$\label{eq:joint-convexity}
 b_{\overline T}(\overline K)
 \le\int_\Omega b_{T_\omega}(K_\omega)\,\,\mathrm d
u(\omega).$$ The right side may be infinite.

For fixed finite arrays and arbitrary positive rates, the energies $e_v$ are smooth in the centers and positive variances. For $s>0$, $$\begin{aligned}
 2\partial_s e_v
 &=\sum_i\alpha_i\partial_{p_i}^2e_v
   -\alpha_vV_v-\sum_{w\ne v}\alpha_wY_{v,w},
   \label{eq:heat-identity}\\
 \partial_{p_{v+1}}\partial_{p_{v-1}}e_v&=Z_v.
   \label{eq:heat-mixed}
\end{aligned}$$ The plane integrals are finite, continuously differentiable in $s$, and twice continuously differentiable in $d$, with $$\label{eq:heat-plane-identities}
 \begin{aligned}
 2\partial_sJ_v(d,s)
 &=\Sigma_\alpha\partial_d^2J_v(d,s)
   -\int_{\Pi_d}\left(\alpha_vV_v+
                  \sum_{w\ne v}\alpha_wY_{v,w}\right)\,\mathrm d\pi_d,\\
 \partial_d^2J_v(d,s)&=\int_{\Pi_d}Z_v\,\,\mathrm d\pi_d.
 \end{aligned}$$ On compact positive scale intervals, the plane integrals of the absolute values of all derivatives used here grow at most polynomially in $|d|$.

For all $d\in\mathbb R$ and all variances $\sigma_v\ge h^2$, $$\label{eq:initial-energy}
 \begin{gathered}
 \int_{\Pi_d}\|W_v\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^3\,\,\mathrm d\pi_d\le M n_v^3,
 \qquad M=1+\sqrt{2/\pi},\\
 \int_{\Pi_d}\sum_ve_v\,\,\mathrm d\pi_d
       \le2\sqrt2 M\sum_v n_v^3.
 \end{gathered}$$ These bounds also hold with the original right-hand sides if any entries are replaced by entries of smaller absolute value.

Let $G_v\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2)$ be complex. At each output pair $(a,b)$, make a step choice of at most $n\ge1$ disjoint radius intervals $(\varepsilon_j,R_j)$ and coefficients $|\beta_j|\le1$. For $$\mathcal K_{a,b}(t)=\sum_j\beta_j I_{\varepsilon_j,R_j}(t)$$ one has $$|\Lambda_{\mathcal K}(G_0,G_1,G_2)|
 \le C\sqrt n\prod_{v=0}^2\|G_v\|_3.$$ The constant is independent of the step partition, the menu of choices, and all endpoints.

Suppose that $c>0$ and that a measurable kernel $f$ satisfies $|f(z)|\le e^{-cz^2}w(z)$, where $w\ge0$ and $\|w\|_5\le\delta$. Then, for every $L>0$, $$\int_{\mathbb R}|F(x+t,y)G(x,y+t)|\,|\mathop{\mathrm{Dil}}_L f(t)|\,\,\mathrm dt \le C_c\delta\,\mathcal M_{F,G}(x,y) \label{eq:gaussian-envelope}$$ at every point where the right side is finite. In particular, a bound $|f(z)|\le A e^{-cz^2}$ gives [eq:gaussian-envelope] with $C_c\delta$ replaced by $C_cA$.

Fix $A\ge1$ and $c>0$. Let $n\ge1$, and let $\mathcal I\subset\mathbb Z$ be finite. For $k\in\mathcal I$, let $K_{a,b,k}\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ and $m_{a,b,k}\in\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$ be finite-valued step choices in $(a,b)$, with $K_{a,b,k}=0$ whenever $m_{a,b,k}=0$. When $m_{a,b,k}\ge1$, suppose that $K_{a,b,k}$ is $C^1$ outside a set of at most $A m_{a,b,k}$ points and that, outside that set, $$|K_{a,b,k}(z)|+|K_{a,b,k}'(z)|\le A e^{-cz^2}.
 \label{eq:rough-family-decay}$$ Assume also that $$\int_{\mathbb R}z^\ell K_{a,b,k}(z)\,\,\mathrm dz=0
 \quad(\ell=0,1,2),
 \qquad
 \sum_{k\in\mathcal I}m_{a,b,k}\le An,
 \quad m_{a,b,k}\le A\sqrt n.
 \label{eq:rough-family-hypotheses}$$ For $$\mathcal K_{a,b}(t)
 =\sum_{k\in\mathcal I}\mathop{\mathrm{Dil}}_{2^k}K_{a,b,k}(t),$$ and smooth compactly supported $G_0,G_1,G_2$, one has $$|\Lambda_{\mathcal K}(G_0,G_1,G_2)|
 \le C_{A,c}\sqrt n\log(2+n)\prod_{v=0}^2\|G_v\|_3.
 \label{eq:rough-family-bound}$$
Proposition 21 remains valid if the three moment conditions in [eq:rough-family-hypotheses] are replaced by the assumption that every $K_{a,b,k}$ is odd almost everywhere.

At each $(a,b)$, choose at most $n$ pairwise disjoint open radius intervals $(\varepsilon_j,R_j)$ with $0<\varepsilon_j<R_j<\infty$, and complex coefficients $\beta_j$ with $|\beta_j|\le1$. Suppose that these choices form a finite-valued step function of $(a,b)$. Then the kernel $$\mathcal E_{a,b}(t)
 =\sum_j\beta_j
       \bigl(E_{\varepsilon_j}(t)-E_{R_j}(t)\bigr)$$ satisfies $$|\Lambda_{\mathcal E}(G_0,G_1,G_2)|
 \le C\sqrt n\log(2+n)\prod_{v=0}^2\|G_v\|_3
 \label{eq:endpoint-error-bound}$$ for smooth compactly supported inputs.
